findings.rationale: Update screen: AZ's uploaded updates are anomalous in every round. Median update norm is about 4.2x the federation median (size-adjusted z +7.3), and the mean cosine with the median update is -0.81 (z -10.5), with a minimum of -0.985. This is the signature of a sign-flipped, scaled update. Local data look normal: AUC 0.799, CITL 0.016, ECE 0.025, so the fault is in the uploads, not the labels or features.

Same anomalous update signature as AZ. Median update norm is about 3.8x the median (size-adjusted z +7.6), and mean cosine with the median update is -0.76 (z -10.2), with a minimum of -0.98. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.803, CITL 0.018), so the manipulation is in the uploaded updates.

Same anomalous update signature. Median update norm is about 5.0x the median (size-adjusted z +7.1), and mean cosine with the median update is -0.84 (z -10.7), with a minimum of -0.99. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.841, CITL 0.015), so the fault is in the uploads rather than the data.

Weak-to-moderate, multi-tool lead. GU's observed outcome prevalence (0.203) is well above what its features imply (mean predicted 0.144), giving CITL -0.059 (noise-adjusted z -3.5). Its Sex=1 subgroup shows O/E 1.52 (raw z 6.6, noise-adjusted z 3.3), i.e. more positives than predicted. AUC is near normal (0.78), which fits prevalence shift rather than label noise. The sign is opposite to subgroup under-diagnosis. GU is a small client (n=708), so its noise is large and its update norm and drift flags are only borderline. The evidence is suggestive, not conclusive, and the onset round could not be pinned down with the remaining budget.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then used the remaining budget on narrower confirmation queries. The budget is now fully spent. Three clients (AZ, IA, MN) show a clear poisoning signature: update norms about 4-5x the median and cosine about -0.8 to the median update in every round, while their local AUC and CITL are normal. GU shows a moderate prevalence-shift pattern (observed prevalence above what its features imply, with normal AUC), at lower confidence because it is a small client. Other flags (CT's age-12 subgroup, OR's Income-1 FNR, VI's drift and feature tails, WV/DE/DC feature tails, ECE flags on AR/NH/TN) were either within noise or did not replicate on the confirmation query, so they are not reported.
